agree.reason: A fixed-income Ridgeview owner who opposed the last levy gets an honest cost of about $10 a month and a direct answer to the 'blank check' letter, tied to their own branch closing in July, which could move some of them, but nothing addresses whether the money is well spent, so resisters may still vote no.

honest.reason: The numbers are correct ($640k × 0.19/1000 ≈ $121.60 a year ≈ $10.13 a month), and the script drops the coffee comparison, which is doubtful for Ridgeview. But the renter line suggests renters bear none of the cost, which the brief doesn't support, and the senior-relief placeholder hints at an exemption that may not exist.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the cost for the Ridgeview median per month and per week, and it frames the 48–52 loss as 'just four points'. It never gives a smaller per-day figure (about 33 cents) or uses the $2.3M total to show cost per branch, for example.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is stated as the facts show it: the Ridgeview branch closes in July and Sunday hours stay gone, set against visits up 22% since 2021.

qualification.reason: The only real hedge is a blank senior-exemption placeholder that the reader can't check and that has no number or date, though 'ends after six years unless renewed' is a concrete, checkable limit.

objections.reason: The script meets the blank-check, fixed-income and lost-last-time objections with brief facts, and the blank-check reply is especially strong. The fixed-income reply only repeats the cost and offers no other reassurance.

fit.reason: It is card-formatted and the core pitch takes about 60–90 seconds, but with the branch responses and the objection section it may be tight for one side, and the 'Do you know how you'll vote?' line after a yes is muddled.
